Linearly interpolate between two scalar values over a duration.

GraphExecutor starts at start_value when simulation time is zero, reaches end_value at duration seconds, and then holds it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | [Signal](../categories/signal.md) |
| Status | Runs |
| Also read from graphs as | `RampSignal` |
| Search words | signal, ramp, simulation |

## Inputs

None: the node starts a branch of the graph.

## Outputs

| Pin | Type | Required | Connections | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Signal** | Tensor | Yes | 1 | Scalar ramp-signal sample |

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ramp | Start value | `start_value` | Number | `0.0` |   | The run | Value at time zero. |
| Ramp | End value | `end_value` | Number | `1.0` |   | The run | Value at the end of the ramp. |
| Ramp | Duration (s) | `duration` | Number | `5.0` | `> 0` | The run | Positive ramp duration in seconds. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Data pipeline (run the graph, **Run step**, previews) | No: RampSignal belongs to the GraphExecutor scalar simulation lane; PipelineExecutor does not execute time-varying simulation sources |

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.
